literal: Lowly association will fear greatness; meanness indeed as kinsmen surrounding will end up.
translation: Greatness dreads and avoids the company of the base; but baseness embraces such company, treating it as its own kin.
modern: பெருமைக் குணம் உடையவர்கள் சிற்றினத்தைக் கண்டு அஞ்சுவார்கள்; ஆனால் சிறுமைக் குணம் உடையவர்களோ அதையே தங்களுக்குச் சுற்றமாக ஏற்றுத் தழுவிக் கொள்வார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts how noble and ignoble minds react to bad company (சிற்றினம்). Greatness of character (பெருமை) instinctively fears and avoids association with low-minded people, knowing its corrupting influence. On the other hand, baseness of character (சிறுமை) naturally welcomes such low association, embracing it closely as if it were its own family (சுற்றமா). The poet uses personification to show that our natural affinities reveal our true character.
